_comment: Curated recurring ANNUAL events that earn an evergreen page at /{metro}/annual/{slug}/ (kids build only). These pages hold search rank year-round ('<name> 2027' queries start weeks before dates are announced) while dated event pages come and go with the 410 lifecycle. `match` is a case-insensitive regex tested against live event titles to cross-link the current year's event page when it exists. Add entries during weekly prep when a verified one-off is clearly an annual tradition; keep descriptions evergreen (no years, no dates beyond the typical month).

bay-area.title: Hayes Valley Carnival
bay-area.description: A free neighborhood carnival that has run for over a century in Hayes Valley: games and prizes along Hayes Street, food, and a one-ring circus performance on the PROXY stage. One of San Francisco's oldest continuous community traditions.

bay-area.title: Bastille Day SF Festival
bay-area.description: The Bay Area's largest celebration of France's national day: French food, music, petanque games, a waiters' race, and family activities on Embarcadero Plaza, held the weekend closest to July 14.

bay-area.title: Japan Day
bay-area.description: Japantown's summer cultural festival from GenRyu Arts: taiko drumming, awa odori street dance, karate demonstrations, and hands-on origami and calligraphy workshops around the outdoor stage at Post and Laguna.

bay-area.title: Teddy Bear Picnic Day at Fairyland
bay-area.description: Children's Fairyland invites every kid to bring their favorite stuffed animal for a day of rides, storytimes, live shows, and the fluffiest picnic in Oakland — a mid-summer Fairyland tradition.

bay-area.title: Alameda County Fair
bay-area.description: One of the Bay Area's biggest county fairs: carnival rides, livestock barns, horse racing, concerts, and fair food across several weeks at the Pleasanton fairgrounds.

chicago.title: Fiesta del Sol
chicago.description: The largest free Latino festival in the country, filling a mile of Cermak Road in Pilsen with live entertainment, food, carnival rides, and a dedicated children's area every summer for over 50 years.

chicago.title: Chinatown Summer Fair
chicago.description: Chinatown's signature street fair: a lion dance procession, kung fu demonstrations, restaurant samplings, cultural performances, and a children's area along Wentworth Avenue.

chicago.title: Chicago Gospel Music Festival
chicago.description: A free weekend of national gospel headliners and local choirs at the Jay Pritzker Pavilion in Millennium Park — family-friendly and one of the city's longest-running free music festivals.

seattle.title: Bite of Seattle
seattle.description: Seattle's summer food festival at Seattle Center: hundreds of food vendors, dozens of musical acts, and free admission, running since 1982.

seattle.title: Seafair Torchlight Parade
seattle.description: Seafair's signature evening parade: illuminated floats, marching bands, drill teams, and dragon dancers along the waterfront — a Seattle summer tradition since 1950.

seattle.title: Whidbey Island Fair
seattle.description: A century-old island county fair in Langley: 4-H animal shows, carnival rides, live music, and a small-town Saturday parade.

seattle.title: Seattle Outdoor Theater Festival
seattle.description: A free weekend of outdoor performance in Volunteer Park — a dozen-plus theater companies playing Shakespeare, family shows, and youth workshops across the lawns.

new-york-city.title: Thunderbird American Indian Powwow
new-york-city.description: New York's largest and longest-running powwow: intertribal dance competitions with dancers from dozens of Indian Nations, plus Native art, craft, and food vendors on the Queens Farm meadow.

los-angeles.title: Alondra Park Ho'olaule'a
los-angeles.description: California's largest free Hawaiian festival: live hula, island music, traditional food, and cultural booths filling Alondra Park each summer.

boston.title: Puerto Rican Festival of Massachusetts
boston.description: A multi-day celebration of Puerto Rican culture in Franklin Park: live performances, traditional food, carnival rides, and family activities, drawing tens of thousands each summer.

boston.title: Revere Beach International Sand Sculpting Festival
boston.description: The East Coast's largest sand sculpting festival: world-class sculptors compete on America's first public beach, with a kids' zone, food vendors, and evening fireworks.

boston.title: Minuteman Library Crawl
boston.description: A week-long summer scavenger hunt across the Minuteman Library Network: pick up a free passport at any participating library, then visit libraries across Greater Boston on their featured crawl days, find each library's hidden clue, and collect stamps. Completed passports enter a grand-prize drawing. Around two dozen libraries take part, from Arlington and Watertown to Natick, Needham and Newton — a free, all-ages tradition that turns library-hopping into a family road trip.

atlanta.title: Atlanta Ice Cream & Wellness Festival
atlanta.description: A free summer Saturday in Piedmont Park combining ice cream vendors with family fitness: live music, yoga and Zumba sessions, wellness screenings, and children's activities.

austin.title: Zilker Summer Musical
austin.match: zilker summer musical|singin' in the rain
austin.description: Austin's free outdoor summer musical tradition since 1959: a full Broadway-style production on the Zilker Hillside Theater lawn, Thursday through Sunday nights all summer. Bring a blanket and picnic.

austin.title: Brick Rodeo
austin.description: The Texas LEGO fan convention: hundreds of custom builds and displays from fan builders, with public exhibition days for families.
